candidates.summary: the new /u/ gate is never reached for `/u/<name>/`, so a registered user's profile 404s on a trailing slash
candidates.failure_scenario: ServeHTTP's dispatch tests `gnourl.IsDir()` (handler_http.go:443) before `gnourl.IsUser()` (line 448), and IsDir is true for any path ending in `/`. Measured against the in-memory node at the head sha: `GET /u/moul001` returns 200 with the profile ("Gnome moul001"), `GET /u/moul001/` returns 404 with a generic body that does not even carry the branch's own "user not found" text. Same for an address: `/u/g1manfred47kzduec920z88wfr64ylksmdcedlf5` 200, `/u/g1manfred47kzduec920z88wfr64ylksmdcedlf5/` 404. A browser or a pasted link that carries the trailing slash loses the profile. The dispatch is not in the diff, so this predates the branch; it is in scope because this PR is the change that defines which /u/ URLs serve a profile, and its own rejection matrix (TestHTTPHandler_GetUserView_RejectsInvalidNames) enumerates /u/foo/bar, /u/a--b, /u/a- and a 65-char name but never the trailing-slash shape.
candidates.verify_by: go test ./gno.land/pkg/gnoweb/ -run TestReachB1UserGateShapes -v with tests/b1-reach-r2-user-url-shapes.go copied into gno.land/pkg/gnoweb/; compare the `/u/moul001` and `/u/moul001/` rows
candidates.evidence: REACH /u/moul001  status=200 body=USER PAGE SERVED / REACH /u/moul001/ status=404 body=- / REACH /u/g1manfred47kzduec920z88wfr64ylksmdcedlf5 status=200 body=USER PAGE SERVED / REACH /u/g1manfred47kzduec920z88wfr64ylksmdcedlf5/ status=404 body=-

candidates.summary: gnoweb's own @mention rule and the /u/ gate this diff installs disagree in both directions, so gnoweb emits /u/ links its handler 404s and never links names the gate accepts
candidates.failure_scenario: mentionNamePattern is `^@([A-Za-z0-9_]{3,90})(?:[^A-Za-z0-9_-]|$)`; the new gate is `gno.Re_name` plus maxUsernameLen 64 (handler_http.go:546-548, 608). Producer-side: the mention parser links consecutive underscores, a leading digit or underscore, and names 65-90 chars, all of which Re_name or the length cap rejects, so the link renders and the page now answers 404 "user not found" where it used to render a blank profile; the repository's own golden output pins one, markdown/golden/ext_mentions/user_mentions.md.txtar:13 emits `<a href="/u/user_with_many_________underscores_and_numbers_12345">`. Consumer-side: Re_name accepts `-` between alphanumerics and the node's own namespace rule (reUserNamespace, gno.land/pkg/sdk/vm/keeper.go:1665, `^[~_a-zA-Z0-9/-]+$`) accepts it too, but the mention pattern's trailing `[^A-Za-z0-9_-]` guard makes `@foo-bar` unmatchable, so a registered user whose name carries a hyphen has a working profile that no mention in any realm ever links to.
candidates.verify_by: grep the golden file for the underscore link, then GET that path against the head handler and observe 404 "user not found"; and check `@foo-bar` against mentionNamePattern in markdown/ext_mentions_test.go
candidates.evidence: user_mentions.md.txtar carries 2 lines with the `_________` run; gno.land/pkg/sdk/vm/keeper.go:1665 reUserNamespace = ^[~_a-zA-Z0-9/-]+$

candidates.summary: buildContributions runs before the isAddress short-circuit, so every /u/<address> page spends a vm/qpaths round trip on a prefix that can never match
candidates.failure_scenario: GetUserView computes isAddress at line 607 and then calls buildContributions unconditionally at 612, with prefix `@` + the bech32 address. On the node, QueryPaths (gno.land/pkg/sdk/vm/keeper.go, the `@` branch) turns that into the prefixes `<domain>/r/g1.../` and `<domain>/p/g1.../`; a package path's second segment is a namespace granted by r/sys/names and can never be address-shaped, so the answer is structurally empty. Live confirmation on rpc.gno.land: `vm/qpaths @g1manfred47kzduec920z88wfr64ylksmdcedlf5` returns an empty data field. Every address profile therefore pays one RPC slot (rpcSlots is a bounded semaphore) and one node store scan for an answer the code already knows, and renders PackageCount/RealmCount/PureCount as a hard zero rather than as 'not applicable'. Moving the call under `if !isAddress` costs nothing the address branch uses.
candidates.verify_by: gnokey query vm/qpaths --data '@g1manfred47kzduec920z88wfr64ylksmdcedlf5' -remote https://rpc.gno.land:443, then read the `@` branch of QueryPaths in gno.land/pkg/sdk/vm/keeper.go

dropped.summary: the node's `@std`/`@stdlibs` special case in QueryPaths returns the whole standard library, so /u/std would clear `len(contribs) == 0` and bypass the existence gate
dropped.settled_by: gnokey query vm/qpaths --data '@std' returns 49 bare names (`bufio`, `chain/banker`, ...) with no leading slash; weburl.ParseFromURL rejects them on reURLPath `^/[a-z0-9_/-]*$`, so every one is skipped and contribs stays empty. Run: REACH /u/std status=404 body=user-not-found, REACH /u/stdlibs status=404 body=user-not-found

dropped.summary: the handler's name gate is looser than the node's own namespace rule, so a name passing it makes ListPaths return `invalid username format` and the page becomes an error view instead of a 404
dropped.settled_by: gno.land/pkg/sdk/vm/keeper.go:1665 reUserNamespace = `^[~_a-zA-Z0-9/-]+$`, which is strictly looser than gno.Re_name; no string Re_name accepts can fail it.

dropped.settled_by: moul001 and zoo_ma123 are registration txs in gno.land/genesis/genesis_txs.jsonl and own no packages, so TestRoutes' `{"/u/moul001", ok, "moul001"}` drives ListPaths empty then a real vm/qeval. dropped.summary: maxUsernameLen 64 is an off-by-one: a 64-character name is rejected or a 65-character one admitted
dropped.settled_by: Run: REACH /u/<64 a's> status=404 body=user-not-found and REACH /u/<65 a's> status=404 body=user-not-found. The 64-char name clears the gate and 404s from the registry lookup, the 65-char one 404s at the gate; the boundary is where the constant says.
